newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T gains after U.S. court ruling.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T gains after U.S. court ruling.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc rose in early trade on Tuesday after a U.S. court cleared R.J. Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco, of responsibility for the death of a smoker who died of lung cancer.

With U.S. tobacco shares up sharply after the verdict, B.A.T shares were quoted up 21p at 542-1/2 by 0715 GMT. On Wall Street, Philip Morris Cos Inc on Monday rose $3-7/8 to $44 and RJR Nabisco gained $3 to $32-5/8.

The Florida jury found that Reynolds was not negligent, in a closely-watched wrongful death verdict that could strengthen the industry's position in talks with a group of state attorneys aimed at settling litigation and other issues.

However the state attorneys said the Florida verdict would not affect their talks with the tobacco industry, arguing that it applied to an individual case and would not affect their attempt to recoup public costs of treating smoking-related illnesses.

A spokesman for B.A.T pointed out that that it was not directly involved in the Florida case, but said the verdict supported its view that a verdict against its U.S. unit Brown & Williamson last year was an aberration.
He said it increased B.A.T's hopes that the verdict against Brown & Williamson would be overturned on appeal later this year.
However the spokesman declined comment on the industry's negotiations with U.S. state attorneys.
Imperial Tobacco Plc, the UK's other tobacco stock, was up 7-1/2p at 409 by 0730 GMT, though it has no direct presence in the U.S. market.
